failures.evidence: A POST that decides nothing still writes `last_decision_at`, so the field can report a decision the broker never made and step 3's gate (and dispatch://INFRA-879's R1, which reads the same field) can open with no decision ever recorded. `ServeDecide` calls `p.recordDecision` once per POST whatever each record became of it (packages/envoy/internal/broker/approval/page.go:418), and `decide` returns "already decided", "expired", "no such record" or "refused: …" without anything being decided (page.go:424-450). The ordinary way to reach it needs no forging: a browser resend of the decision form it already sent — a second click, a back-and-resubmit, a retried request. Observed on the live binary at 127.0.0.1:17777, signed in as alice@example.com through the real code flow: `last_decision_at` 2026-10-31T11:03:56.974325Z after the real approval, then 2026-10-31T11:03:59.076438Z after resending the identical form, whose broker log line reads `outcome="already decided"`; the record stayed granted with one grant. The same POST shape from a signed-in person who is not the approver (carol@example.com, page token computed from her own session cookie) also moved it, with the record left pending and `outcome="refused: …"`. A request that expires while its page is open is the same case and needs no second click at all. Red test: `TestSignInStatusWritesNoDecisionWhenThePostDecidedNothing` in packages/envoy/internal/broker/approval/status_test.go, committed at 51ed20ff124c. No existing test pins the current behaviour, so nothing has to be deleted to fix it: record the decision only when at least one record was actually decided.

observationsForTheReviewer: Not a failure, but a comment that is wrong where it matters: packages/envoy/internal/broker/approval/page.go:179-181 says a visitor with no session "gets the same redirect whether or not the id exists". It does not — an id that names a record with a person carries that person as login_hint, which A1 requires, and an id no record has carries none. Measured: GET /approve/<a real record> with no session gives `login_hint=alice%40example.com`, GET /approve/<64 random hex> gives none. Record ids are unguessable SHA-256 hashes, so nothing follows from it, but the sentence says the opposite of what the code does and page.go:95-96 repeats it.

packages/envoy/internal/broker/api/handlers_ui_records.go reads the record's kind before it authenticates, so an unauthenticated caller gets 403 DECIDE_ON_BROKER_PAGE for an id that names a secret request and 401 for one that names nothing. The comment at :202-204 says such a caller "learns no more about which ids exist than a machine login's own answer tells it", which is not exactly true; with 64-hex record ids it is not reachable, and the shared per-address bucket is spent first.

A signed-in person of the domain who is not the approver is served the whole record page — the secret names, the requesting enrollment, the reason and the times — with no decision form. That is what the spec's design describes and A2 only requires that she decide nothing, which she does not; naming it here because the plan's D6 had closed a similar disclosure on the machine-login page that spec v24 then dropped.
